questions.q: What are the two main techniques secrets detection tools use to find credentials?
options: Pattern matching and entropy analysis
Taint analysis and code coverage
CVSS scoring and manifest parsing
Container layer diffing and image signing
questions.explain: Pattern matching catches known secret shapes (like an AWS key prefix), while entropy analysis catches high-randomness strings that don't match any known pattern.

questions.q: Why do tools like gitleaks scan git history, not just the current state of the files?
options: Because scanning history is required by GitHub's terms of service
Because a secret committed and later deleted in a new commit is still retrievable from history
Because history scanning is faster than scanning current files
Because current files never contain secrets
questions.explain: Deleting a line in a later commit does not remove it from git history — the secret remains retrievable by anyone who can access past commits, so scanning must cover history too.

questions.q: What is the only real fix once a secret has been pushed to a repository?
options: Deleting the line in the next commit
Rotating the credential — issuing a new one and revoking the old one at its source
Renaming the file that contained it
Making the repository private
questions.explain: Once pushed, a secret must be treated as compromised. The only real fix is rotation: generate a new credential and revoke the old one, regardless of whether the line is later removed.

questions.q: What does GitHub's push protection do differently from standard secret scanning alerts?
options: It scans container images instead of source code
It blocks a push before GitHub accepts it, if the push matches a known secret pattern
It only works on private repositories
It automatically rotates any credential it finds
questions.explain: Push protection intervenes before the push is accepted, preventing the secret from ever reaching the shared branch — standard secret scanning alerts fire only after the fact.

questions.q: In the example gitleaks finding, what does the "Entropy" field indicate?
options: How many times the secret has been used in production
A measure of how random the matched string is, used to judge whether it resembles a generated secret
The number of commits that reference the file
The CVSS severity score of the finding
questions.explain: Entropy is a randomness score — high entropy is characteristic of a generated credential rather than ordinary text, and it's one of the signals a scanner uses to flag a finding.
